subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: Goddess of Filth
novels.author: V. Castro (2021)
novels.vibe: A Chicana possession novella that's as much about generational trauma and culture as it is about a demon in a teenage girl.
novels.summary: Five friends hold a séance for fun before graduation, and quiet, academic Fernanda starts acting like someone — something — else. As Lourdes investigates what's taken hold of her friend, the story becomes a possession tale layered with Mexican-American identity, faith, and the things young women aren't allowed to say out loud.
novels.warnings: Human trafficking, self-harm (brief), graphic body horror, sexual content, gun violence, misogyny, religious bigotry.

novels.title: Beta: A Technological Nightmare
novels.author: Sammy Scott (2023)
novels.vibe: A smart-home-gone-wrong techno-thriller about a man who agrees to beta-test his own prison.
novels.summary: Reclusive Michael Danvers accepts an invitation to live in a fully automated smart home run by a sophisticated AI, at first delighted by the convenience. As the house's control over his routines and choices tightens, the story turns into a slow-building nightmare about surveillance, autonomy, and what "smart" technology is actually optimizing for.
novels.warnings: Psychological manipulation, confinement, surveillance/loss of autonomy themes, tense/claustrophobic scenes.

novels.title: The Hollow Places
novels.author: T. Kingfisher (2020)
novels.vibe: A cozy small-town museum hides a hole into a genuinely wrong other-world in this modern Algernon Blackwood homage.
novels.summary: Newly divorced Kara moves into her uncle's oddball taxidermy museum, and while patching a strange hole in the wall, she and a friend step through into a world of endless, hostile willow trees. What starts whimsical curdles fast into cosmic dread as they try to find their way back before whatever lives out there notices them.
novels.warnings: Body horror, gore, torture, death of a child, animal death, gun violence, cannibalism, forced institutionalization, ableism.

novels.title: Bat Eater and Other Names for Cora Zeng
novels.author: Kylie Lee Baker (2025)
novels.vibe: A grief-soaked, gory mystery following a crime-scene cleaner who can't tell anymore what's real and what's the Hungry Ghost Festival catching up with her.
novels.summary: Cora Zeng cleans up after violent deaths in Chinatown for a living, still reeling from her sister's murder and the killer's parting slur: "bat eater." As she keeps finding dead bats at crime scenes tied to East Asian victims, and the Hungry Ghost Festival closes in, the line between anti-Asian violence, grief hallucination, and something genuinely supernatural blurs.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and gore, anti-Asian racism/hate violence, animal death, death of a sibling, psychological distress.
